body: the general classification of these files are msbuild specific files, i didn't see a reason to break it out right now

While I now understand why these changes were necessary/correct, I spent about 30 minutes being very confused over what was going on here.

Could we leave a comment (either at the top of the dotnet test module or at the first time it's used) explaining why this form is the correct output to expect, and isn't just us breaking the tests so that the version doesn't need to display?

Alternatively, is there a way we could make this match better, e.g. by employing a regex in testing so that we at least know we're getting valid version numbers on the end and not random strings?
i could add a regex to this to make it more robust. i'm dabbling for the first time with rust for this so it'll take me a bit.

I think you would need to add the regex into the `expect_output` function, so that instead of checking for a substring match, it checks for substring + version-number-looking-thing.

Fortunately, [we already use the regex crate](https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/master/Cargo.toml#L55) so you can just use/import it in the tests.
@chipbuster great thanks! i just refactored to account for a pattern string to being passed to the `expect_output` function. ill get the formatting fixed in a jiffy
